Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 1) A wound is best defined as:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option3: Disruption of the normal anatomical continuity of tissue
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: A wound is any break in the normal structure of tissues caused by trauma or surgery.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 2) Which of the following is a clean wound?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option2: Penetrating abdominal injury with bowel perforation
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Clean wounds are uninfected operative wounds in which no hollow viscus is entered.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 3) Which class of wound has the highest risk of surgical site infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Dirty wounds contain established infection or devitalized tissue before operation.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 4) Healing of a clean surgical incision with well-approximated edges occurs by:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Primary intention occurs when wound edges are accurately approximated with minimal tissue loss.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 5) Healing by secondary intention is characterized by:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option2: Granulation tissue formation with wound contraction
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Secondary intention occurs in wounds with tissue loss or infection.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 6) Delayed primary closure is usually performed:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option4: After 3–5 days when contamination is controlled
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Delayed primary closure combines infection control with later wound closure.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 7) The first phase of wound healing is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Haemostasis and inflammation begin immediately after injury.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 8) Which cell predominates during the early inflammatory phase of wound healing?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Neutrophils are the first inflammatory cells to reach the wound.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 9) Fibroblasts become prominent during:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Fibroblasts synthesize collagen and extracellular matrix during proliferation.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 10) The principal collagen deposited during early wound healing is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Type III collagen is laid down first and is later replaced by Type I collagen.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 11) Which collagen predominates in a mature scar?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Remodeling gradually replaces Type III collagen with stronger Type I collagen.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 12) Wound contraction is mainly produced by:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Myofibroblasts reduce wound size by contracting the wound edges.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 13) The strongest risk factor for postoperative wound infection is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Diabetes impairs leukocyte function and delays wound healing.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 14) Which vitamin deficiency most commonly delays collagen synthesis?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Vitamin C is essential for collagen hydroxylation.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 15) Zinc deficiency primarily affects:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Zinc is required for protein synthesis and tissue repair.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 16) The commonest organism causing surgical site infection is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: S. aureus remains the leading cause of surgical wound infection.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 17) Which sign is most suggestive of wound infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Purulent discharge strongly suggests bacterial wound infection.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 18) The commonest cause of wound dehiscence is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Infection weakens wound strength and predisposes to dehiscence.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 19) Complete disruption of all layers of an abdominal wound with protrusion of bowel is called:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Burst abdomen is a surgical emergency requiring prompt management.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 20) Which of the following is NOT a local factor delaying wound healing?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Hypothyroidism is a systemic factor; the others are local factors affecting wound healing.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 21) The tensile strength of a healing wound reaches its maximum at:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option4: It never reaches the strength of normal tissue
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Even after complete healing, scar tissue usually achieves about 70–80% of the tensile strength of normal skin.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 22) Which phase of wound healing is characterized by collagen remodeling?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: During maturation, collagen fibers are reorganized, increasing wound strength.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 23) Which cell is primarily responsible for collagen synthesis?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Fibroblasts produce collagen and extracellular matrix during wound healing.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 24) Which growth factor plays the greatest role in angiogenesis during wound healing?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) promotes formation of new blood vessels.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 25) Healthy granulation tissue appears:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Healthy granulation tissue is well vascularized and has a bright red appearance.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 26) Which organism is most commonly responsible for gas gangrene?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Clostridium perfringens produces exotoxins that cause rapid muscle necrosis and gas formation.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 27) The characteristic feature of gas gangrene is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Gas production within tissues produces palpable crepitus.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 28) The definitive treatment of gas gangrene is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Early radical debridement is essential to remove devitalized tissue.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 29) Necrotizing fasciitis most commonly involves:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: The infection spreads rapidly along fascial planes.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 30) The commonest organism causing necrotizing fasciitis is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Group A β-haemolytic streptococcus is a major cause of necrotizing fasciitis.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 31) The treatment of necrotizing fasciitis includes:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: Broad-spectrum antibiotics and urgent surgical debridement
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Early surgery is the most important life-saving intervention.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 32) Which of the following is the commonest hospital-acquired wound infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Surgical site infection is one of the commonest healthcare-associated infections.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 33) Which of the following is classified as a clean-contaminated wound?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Controlled entry into the gastrointestinal or biliary tract without significant contamination is clean-contaminated.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 34) Which of the following is a contaminated wound?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Fresh accidental wounds and operations with major breaks in aseptic technique are contaminated wounds.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 35) Which wound class has the lowest infection rate?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Clean wounds have the lowest incidence of postoperative infection.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 36) Which of the following is the most important local factor promoting wound infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Dead space allows accumulation of blood and fluid, promoting bacterial growth.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 37) Which microorganism commonly causes postoperative wound infection after colorectal surgery?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Enteric Gram-negative organisms commonly infect colorectal surgical wounds.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 38) Which type of suture is preferred for infected wounds?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Monofilament sutures harbor fewer bacteria than braided sutures.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 39) A sinus is best defined as:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option3: An abnormal communication between two epithelial surfaces
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option4: A blind tract opening onto the skin
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: A sinus has one external opening and ends blindly.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 40) A fistula is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: A communication between two epithelial-lined surfaces
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Fistulas connect two epithelial surfaces or an epithelial surface and the skin.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 41) Which of the following is the commonest cause of a chronic discharging sinus?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Chronic osteomyelitis commonly presents with a persistent discharging sinus.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 42) Which organism is classically associated with hospital-acquired MRSA infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: MRSA is an important cause of healthcare-associated surgical wound infection.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 43) The commonest source of bacteria causing postoperative wound infection is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Most surgical site infections arise from the patient’s own skin or endogenous flora.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 44) Which of the following favors wound infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Haematoma provides an excellent medium for bacterial growth.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 45) The most appropriate treatment for a fluctuant abscess is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Pus must be drained; antibiotics alone are usually insufficient.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 46) The classical signs of acute inflammation include all except:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: The classical signs are redness, heat, swelling, pain and loss of function.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 47) Which organism is the commonest cause of cellulitis?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Group A Streptococcus is the most frequent cause of diffuse cellulitis.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 48) Erysipelas primarily involves the:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Erysipelas is a superficial streptococcal skin infection with well-defined margins.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 49) Cellulitis differs from erysipelas because cellulitis:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option2: Involves deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Cellulitis is a deeper infection with poorly defined margins.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 50) The commonest causative organism of boils (furuncles) is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Furuncles are acute infections of hair follicles caused predominantly by S. aureus.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 51) A carbuncle is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option2: Infection of a single sweat gland
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Carbuncles consist of multiple furuncles connected beneath the skin.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 52) Carbuncles occur most commonly in:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Diabetes mellitus predisposes to recurrent staphylococcal skin infections.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 53) Which of the following is the treatment of choice for a mature carbuncle?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option3: Incision and drainage with antibiotics if indicated
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Adequate drainage is essential for successful treatment.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 54) The most common organism causing an infected sebaceous cyst is:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Secondary bacterial infection of sebaceous cysts is usually caused by S. aureus.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 55) Which of the following delays wound healing the most?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Oxygen is essential for collagen synthesis, angiogenesis and bacterial killing.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 56) Which patient has the highest risk of wound dehiscence?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option3: Malnourished elderly diabetic with wound infection
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Multiple risk factors act synergistically to impair wound healing.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 57) Which of the following is the strongest suture-holding layer of the abdominal wall?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: The fascia provides the main tensile strength of abdominal wound closure.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 58) Evisceration refers to:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option3: Protrusion of abdominal viscera through a disrupted wound
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Evisceration is a surgical emergency requiring immediate management.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 59) Which complication is most likely after premature removal of skin sutures?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Removing sutures too early may result in separation of wound edges.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 60) Which statement regarding wound healing is correct?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: Wound healing depends on both local and systemic factors.
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option3: Vitamin C has no role in wound healing.
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option4: Scar tissue becomes stronger than normal skin.
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Local factors (infection, blood supply, foreign body) and systemic factors (nutrition, diabetes, age, medications) together determine the rate and quality of wound healing.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 61) Which type of collagen predominates in mature scar tissue?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: During remodeling, Type III collagen is gradually replaced by stronger Type I collagen.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 62) Which of the following is the commonest cause of stitch abscess?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option4: Local bacterial contamination around suture material
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Stitch abscess usually develops around infected or reactive suture material.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 63) Which patient is most likely to develop a keloid?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Keloids occur more commonly in young individuals with darker skin pigmentation.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 64) Keloid differs from hypertrophic scar because it:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: Remains confined within the wound margins
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option4: Extends beyond the original wound margins
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Keloids grow beyond the wound edges and have a high recurrence rate after excision.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 65) Hypertrophic scar is characterized by:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option4: Remaining within the original wound boundaries
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Hypertrophic scars are raised scars confined to the original wound.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 66) Which of the following is the treatment of choice for a small hypertrophic scar?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option2: Silicone gel sheet or pressure therapy
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Conservative treatment is effective for many hypertrophic scars.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 67) Which factor is least likely to contribute to surgical site infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Proper haemostasis reduces haematoma formation and lowers infection risk.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 68) Which microorganism commonly causes postoperative wound infection after vascular surgery?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Gram-positive cocci, especially S. aureus, commonly infect clean surgical wounds.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 69) Which of the following is an indication for delayed primary closure?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Delayed primary closure allows infection to be controlled before wound closure.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 70) Which of the following is the most appropriate management of a contaminated traumatic wound?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: Irrigation, debridement and delayed closure if necessary
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Thorough wound toilet and removal of devitalized tissue reduce infection risk.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 71) The most important principle of wound debridement is removal of:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Necrotic tissue promotes bacterial growth and delays healing.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 72) Which solution is most commonly used for irrigation of traumatic wounds?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Copious irrigation with normal saline effectively removes debris while minimizing tissue damage.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 73) Which wound is most suitable for healing by primary intention?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Primary intention requires clean wounds with well-approximated edges.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 74) Which condition predisposes most strongly to chronic non-healing ulcers?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Poor arterial blood supply significantly impairs tissue repair.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 75) Which of the following is the earliest microscopic event in wound healing?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Haemostasis begins immediately after injury with platelet plug formation.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 76) Macrophages are important in wound healing because they:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: Remove debris and release growth factors
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Macrophages coordinate repair by phagocytosis and cytokine production.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 77) Which phase of wound healing is characterized by maximum angiogenesis?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Granulation tissue formation during proliferation is rich in newly formed capillaries.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 78) Which of the following is a systemic factor affecting wound healing?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Diabetes impairs immune function, collagen synthesis and microcirculation.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 79) Which patient has the greatest risk of pressure ulcer formation?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Prolonged pressure and immobility predispose to pressure ulcers.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 80) Which measure is most effective in preventing pressure sores?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Regular pressure relief is the cornerstone of pressure sore prevention.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 81) Which microorganism is most commonly responsible for bite wound infection after a dog bite?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Pasteurella multocida is the commonest pathogen isolated from dog and cat bite wounds.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 82) Which wound is least suitable for immediate primary closure?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Infected wounds require drainage and debridement before considering closure.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 83) Which of the following is the most important principle in managing animal bite wounds?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Copious irrigation markedly reduces bacterial contamination and infection.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 84) Human bite wounds are particularly prone to infection because of:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: Mixed aerobic and anaerobic oral flora
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Human saliva contains numerous pathogenic organisms, making these wounds highly contaminated.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 85) Which of the following is the most common organism causing human bite wound infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Eikenella corrodens is characteristically associated with human bite injuries.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 86) Which wound should generally be left open after initial management?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Infected bite wounds are usually managed with delayed closure to reduce infection risk.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 87) Which condition most strongly predisposes to necrotizing soft tissue infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Diabetes impairs immunity and increases susceptibility to severe soft tissue infections.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 88) Which feature is most suggestive of necrotizing fasciitis?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option2: Pain out of proportion to physical findings
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Severe disproportionate pain is an early hallmark of necrotizing fasciitis.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 89) Which investigation is most useful for confirming gas in soft tissues?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Soft tissue gas may be demonstrated on plain radiographs in gas-forming infections.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 90) Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be useful as an adjunct in:
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Hyperbaric oxygen may inhibit anaerobic organisms but never replaces surgical debridement.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 91) Which of the following is the best indicator of successful wound healing?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option3: Restoration of tensile strength with epithelialization
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Healing is assessed by progressive epithelialization and increasing wound strength.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 92) Which of the following is the most common complication of untreated wound infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Persistent infection weakens collagen and predisposes to wound separation.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 93) Which of the following promotes bacterial proliferation within a wound?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Necrotic tissue serves as an excellent medium for bacterial growth.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 94) Which is the most effective method of preventing surgical site infection?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option2: Strict aseptic technique with meticulous tissue handling
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Gentle tissue handling and aseptic principles remain the cornerstone of infection prevention.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 95) Which type of drain is commonly used for passive wound drainage?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Corrugated drains allow passive drainage by gravity and capillary action.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 96) Which of the following is an advantage of closed suction drainage?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: Lower infection risk than open drainage
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Closed suction systems reduce retrograde bacterial contamination.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 97) Which of the following wounds is most likely to require skin grafting?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Skin grafting is indicated when primary closure is not possible because of significant tissue loss.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 98) Which of the following is the commonest cause of failure of skin graft take?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Blood collection beneath the graft prevents revascularization and graft adherence.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 99) Which statement regarding wound healing is true?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: Antibiotics alone replace adequate surgical drainage.
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option2: All wounds should be closed primarily.
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option4: Collagen synthesis is complete within 48 hours.
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: Foreign material perpetuates inflammation, increases infection risk and delays tissue repair.

Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.question: 100) Which statement regarding surgical wound management is correct?
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option1: Adequate debridement is more important than immediate wound closure.
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option2: Every contaminated wound should be sutured immediately.
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.option4: Wound infection is best managed with antibiotics alone.
Wounds, Wound Healing & InInfection.exp: The foundation of successful wound management is thorough debridement, irrigation, removal of devitalized tissue and control of contamination before definitive closure.
